notes: In-app updates now actually reload server.js — previously apply-update downloaded the new server.js but 'restarted' with an in-process server.close()+listen(), which keeps the OLD code in memory, so server-side fixes only applied after a full manual quit/relaunch. Now apply-update re-execs a fresh node process (spawn(process.execPath, [process.argv[1], …], { detached:true, env:{…, PORT:activePort} }) + unref, then exit) so the new code is loaded, binding the SAME port the browser is polling. To make the port hand-off reliable, the single-instance guard now also clears the target PORT (not just 3000-3004), and PID-file cleanup only deletes the file when it still holds our own PID (so the successor's entry isn't clobbered on the way out). Safety nets: the new server.js is syntax-checked (node -c) before hand-off — if it fails, the current server keeps running and logs a warning rather than exiting into a dead process; if spawn fails, it falls back to the old in-process re-listen. The client already detects the return via socket reconnect + /ping polling, so no client change was needed. NOTE: this fix bootstraps itself — the FIRST update to v1.4.82 still re-listens under the old logic, so one manual app restart is needed for it to take hold; updates after that re-exec automatically. lsof-based port clearing is macOS/Linux; Windows relies on the cross-platform PID-file SIGTERM. Verified with an isolation harness replicating the guard + respawn: after restart a NEW pid takes over the SAME port with freshly-loaded code (samePort+newCodeLoaded), ~0.5-1s downtime; node -c passes.
